steps.text: Malleability means a material can be beaten or hammered into thin sheets. Let's find out which materials are malleable.
Pick a metal first — tap Copper.
Now tap “Hammer the Material” and watch what happens.
The metal flattens into a thin sheet — its particles slide over each other without breaking. That's malleability.
Now try a non-metal — tap Coal, then hammer it.
It shatters into pieces. Non-metals are brittle: their particles are rigidly bonded, so they break instead of bending. Metals are malleable, non-metals are brittle.

coach.mission: Hammer a metal and a non-metal to see which one is malleable.
whenStuck: Tap a material first, then tap “Hammer the Material”.
Try a metal like Copper, then a non-metal like Coal, and compare.
whenWrong: Metals flatten into sheets (malleable); non-metals break apart (brittle).
If it shattered, that was a non-metal — brittle, not malleable.
whenCorrect: Right — the metal flattened into a sheet, so it's malleable.
Nice — you saw the non-metal shatter because it's brittle.
coach.done: You've seen that metals are malleable and non-metals are brittle. Test more materials, or move on when you're ready.
